_comment_family: Texturina ships as a family of OPTICAL SIZES, and the two files in
fonts/ are two cuts of one of them: this Regular and the Bold beside
it, both from the 18pt instance, both carrying 'Texturina 18pt' as
name ID 1 with the cut left to the subfamily. Asking for 'Texturina
18pt' alone would let either of them answer, and these two are used
TOGETHER on one line - the Bold is what a picked word is set in, so a
Regular answering in its place would leave the highlight identical to
the words either side of it. The full name (name ID 4) is what gets
declared instead, exactly as the two Telegraf and the two Raleway
packs do and for their reason.
The 18pt in that name is the optical size and not an instruction
about how big to set the face: the caption it is used for is set at
the Snapchat preset's 40px like every other caption here. An optical
size says which drawing of the letterforms this is, and the small end
of that axis is the one drawn for READING - sturdier hairlines, more
open spacing, less contrast between thick and thin - while the large
end is drawn for a headline seen whole. The channel that uses this
sets its type straight onto a photograph with no card under it (see
inkjection-fr), which is the hardest ground a serif can be asked to
hold, so the reading cut is the right end of the axis to ship even
though the type is comfortably bigger than 18pt on screen.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Stated rather than left to 'normal' so the pairing with the
700 next door is written down on both halves of it.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and also the name the installer registers the file under when it puts
a copy into Windows (engine.install_fonts takes the first entry, and
Windows keys installed fonts by name ID 4). The first is that full
name and the second the PostScript name; both name this one cut
rather than the family, so a machine answering to either is answering
with a Regular. 'Texturina 18pt' on its own is deliberately absent -
it is the name the Bold answers to as well, and a Bold arriving here
would set the whole block in the highlight's weight.
This fallback is less likely to fire than most in this folder.
Texturina is not a face that comes with Windows or with an office
suite, so on a machine that never ran the installer these names
resolve to nothing and the stack below is what answers.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before anything is
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied.
Georgia first, because it is the one serif on every Windows this app
runs on that was drawn for the same job: reading at text sizes on a
screen, with the sturdy hairlines that survive being laid over a
photograph. Times New Roman behind it is the floor, and it is a
poorer stand-in for exactly that reason - it was drawn for print at
newspaper sizes and its thins go to nothing on screen - but it is
present everywhere and it is at least a serif.
Impact and Arial Black, which most of this folder falls back through,
are absent for telegraf-ultralight's reason turned the other way up:
they are heavy sans display grotesques, and this is a literary serif.
